  Ran 1 shell command

⏺ Found it. The parser walks upward from the last option and stops at the first non-option line:

  for i := last; i >= 0; i-- {
      match := optionLine.FindStringSubmatch(lines[i])
      if match == nil { break }   // ← stops here

  Claude Code's UI puts a description under each option and a horizontal rule before the last one. Let me
  confirm that's the cause:

  Ran 1 shell command

⏺ My hypothesis was wrong — still nil. Let me stop guessing and instrument the detector directly:

  Ran 1 shell command

⏺ Found the actual cause — and it's one line. The footer regex:

  var footerLine = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^\s*(esc to|press |↑/↓|tab to)`)

  Claude Code's footer reads Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel. It starts with "Enter to
  select", which matches none of those alternatives — and the pattern is anchored to line start, so the
  ↑/↓ mid-line doesn't help either. Unrecognised trailing text means "this menu is already resolved", so
  Detect bails.
